column1: # FROZEN 2026-03-17 — legacy CREED (national CRE/CMBS) archive, NOT maintained. Canonical = AGENTS/CREED/STATUS.md + AGENTS/CREED/thesis/THESIS.md. Do NOT cite rows as current: values are Jan–Mar 2026 (e.g. Office CMBS DQ 12.34% Jan -> superseded by 11.57% Jun 2026).

column11: Notes

NEW RECORD. Exceeds prior ATH of 11.76% (Oct 2025). +211 bps YoY. Office the largest contributor to net delinquencies ($1.6B net increase in Jan). Special servicing 17.11% (+47bps MoM, 59% of Jan transfers). Relentless deterioration continues.

RQ-001 RESOLVED. 1.56% (DRCRELEXFACBS) = all banks, all CRE incl owner-occupied. 4.18% (FDIC QBP) = large banks >$250B, non-owner-occupied only = correct CMBS comparator. Masking gap = 7.1pp (vs CMBS office 11.31%). Declining from 4.99% peak (Q3 2024), 4th consecutive decline. Pre-pandemic: 0.59%. Small banks: 1.14% DQ but 1,788 exceed 300% CRE/equity. Mods suppress bank DQ (66% increase through Q2 2025; $39.3B modified balance, +86% YoY).

Rising again after brief Oct peak (7.12%). +232bps YoY = stress spreading beyond office. Sunbelt oversupply: Austin 15.3% vacancy (worst nationally), Atlanta 12%, Phoenix/Nashville ~10-12%. Pipeline collapsing (starts -40%+) = supply relief coming. $115B loans with DSCR <1.20x maturing by end 2026. Two-thirds of MF foreclosures = 2021-22 vintage. RQ-012: MF insurance +119% since pre-pandemic.

RQ-006/011 enriched. BIFURCATION EXTREME: Trophy 12-14% & tightening. Class B 20-25% & flat/worsening. Class C 25-35% & worsening. SF: trophy 15.3% vs overall 35.1% (20pp gap). Manhattan: trophy 55% of leasing (up from 38%). Chicago: trophy rents +26% since 2020 vs market +1%. Trophy = 2-4% of stock. Class B = 40-45%, C = 15-20%. B/C breakeven at ~75-80% occupancy — many at/below. Bottom-tier B/C obsolescence is PERMANENT. CMBS office DQ 11.76% (exceeds GFC peak by 106bps). AI DEMAND: 7M SF in SF (12% of stock), 35% of SF leasing, 80% of newly leased. AI durable 2-3yr but 20-30% contraction risk 2027-28. Structural floor from big tech AI divisions (30-40%). AI is gateway-city positive only — does NOT solve B/C or secondary markets.

RQ-007/008 enriched. UPGRADE TO RED. Bank mods +66% YoY ($16.7B→$27.7B). Securitized +86% YoY. Q3 volume $11.2B. 67% are extensions. Small banks +217% mod rate (vs large +14%). Mods grew 326.9% in 2024. Full payoffs -53.1%. $64.6B in CMBS special servicing (surpassed GFC peak). ASU 2022-02 disclosure cliff Dec 2025 = visibility will DROP as maturity wall peaks. Q4 10-Ks PENDING.

RQ-008 enriched. ~One-third of recent mods re-default. $5.5B re-defaults = decade high. Avg payment relief on re-defaulted mods only ~2% (insufficient). FDIC historical: >30% of modified RE loans subsequently foreclosed. Loss severity on re-defaults: 49.7-63% (far exceeds GFC ~33%). CRED iQ: "early part of the curve." Extensions (67% of mods) don't fix valuation problems. Institutional defaults ($15-20B+) confirm — even Brookfield/PIMCO walk away rather than inject equity.
Awaiting Q4 2025 data. H1 2025: ~150 CRE foreclosures (highest midyear since 2014).

column4: -24% overall CPPI from peak (Dec 2025: -0.1% MoM, +2.3% YoY); Chicago -71% avg
column11: UPGRADE TO RED. Chicago office actual sales: -71% average decline (5 major transactions: -61% to -82.6%). 600 West Chicago $510M→$89M (-82.6%), 70 West Madison $377M→$80M (-78.6%). Validates extreme valuation collapse in secondary markets. Green Street overall CPPI improving but office-specific worse.
Cap rates dipped ~9bps H1 2025. Industrial: 25% of respondents believe past peak. Office still wide.
IMPROVING: Up 17% YoY through 9M 2025. Q3 at $150.6B strongest since 2022. Recovery underway but still 50% below peak.

RQ-002/003 RESOLVED. $936B breakdown: MF ~32% ($300B), Office ~14-20% ($130-187B), Banks ~48% ($452B). 40-50% is 2021-22 vintage. H1 ~$375B / H2 ~$560B. Refi gap: base case $336B (36%); realistic capacity $500-700B. Forced recognition $140-250B over 2026-27. 30-40% fail DSCR at 1.25x (148bps rate gap = 16.3% DS increase). 20-30% of wall is extended loans. 1,788 banks >300% CRE/equity. Each 50bps Fed cut = $50-75B additional capacity. Office 20-30% foreclosure rate. NOT 2008 but largest forced recognition since GFC.

column4: Office: only 44% paid on time; 51% outstanding past maturity. SB default rate 12.9% (office 19.7%)
column11: RQ-007/009 enriched. UPGRADE TO RED. Only 44% of 2025 office maturities paid on time (vs 72% all property). 51% still outstanding past maturity. KBRA SB default rate: 12.9% (doubled from 6.4%); office 19.7% (up from 1.9% = 10x). JPM estimate: ~$39B CMBS office (21%) will default. Loss severity 49.7-63% (far exceeds GFC). Institutional strategic defaults accelerating ($15-20B+). Peak expected H1 2026.

RP-CREED-9 COMPLETE. CMBS office lease wall: 2024 (112M), 2025 (105-150M), 2026 (92-110M), 2027 (50-110M), 2028 (415M = CRISIS YEAR). NYC: 173M sf (32M in 2024-25). Top 10 MSAs = 61% of expirations. 161M sf (19%) are single-tenant properties. Space contraction on renewal: -21% (avg renewals), -32% (new deals), -48% (Fannie Mae case). Non-renewal + downsizing creates NOI collapse → extend-and-pretend FAILS because leases cannot be extended. 2028 is unavoidable reckoning. Thesis: "It's not a refinancing crisis, it's a demand collapse disguised as a maturity wall."

column4: $130-217B (improving: BREIT gates lifted, ODCE positive returns)
column11: RQ-010 enriched. BREIT meeting all redemptions since early 2024 = positive. ODCE had 3 consecutive quarters positive total return. But: SREIT NAV -40% from peak ($8.8B), $999M redemption queue (11.6% NAV), only 3-4% fulfilled, redemption limits cut to 0.33%/month. Moody's downgraded Blackstone (Ba2→Ba3), Apollo, KKR CRE funds — rising problem loans. CRE debt outperforming equity: 2022 vintage 11.3% median IRR (debt) vs 2.1% (equity). Non-traded REIT sector: $2.8B redemption requests vs $1.2B inflows (Q1 2025). FSB (Jun 2025): non-bank CRE investors "could amplify financial risks in a downturn."

column4: Declining (BREIT gates lifted; ODCE queues shrinking via rescissions)
column11: IMPROVING: BREIT gates fully lifted. ODCE queues declining as returns turned positive. High rescission rates = investors choosing to stay. Peaked at 19.3% (worse than GFC's 15%).

RQ-010 enriched. Market reopened dramatically. Jan 2025 alone $5.4B (more than half of 2024 total $8.7B). Total CMBS+CLO issuance $125.6B in 2025 (+21% YoY). BUT underlying quality diverging: CRE CLO non-performing matured loans at 43% of matured balances (+720bps surge). 66.3% of allocated CRE CLO loan balances ($3.8B) in matured loans. 76% of floating-rate CRE CLO is MF. SMBC provides ~90% of rate cap agreements (concentration risk). 40% of rate caps expire before loan maturity (~700 loans/$30B+). Record Q2 2025 issuance ($8.9B) = new vintage confidence despite legacy distress. Bifurcation: legacy CLOs distressed, new issuance healthy.

RQ-005 enriched. Crisis is self-reinforcing cycle. 1,438 FL buildings on Fannie blacklist (doubled in 2yr; ~700 in South FL). FL #1 nationally in foreclosures — 8 consecutive months rising (+57% YoY). Condo prices -9.9% YoY (worst since 2009). 7 of 10 worst US metros are FL. Cape Coral -31% from peak (below 2006 bubble). Insurance +164% (Miami-Dade). ~28K associations, ~1.5M units. FHA DQ >11%. Super-lien subordinates mortgages. Buildings <30yr +10% value; >30yr severe declines. Bank exposure UNQUANTIFIED.

UPGRADE FROM GREEN. NYC: 4.1M sf through Aug 2025 (2.5x 2024). Policy support expanding (NYC 90% tax exemptions, DC 20yr abatements). 10-15% of office buildings suitable. Becoming a material supply-side factor for vacancy relief.

column4: Office: under 20M sf (lowest in 21st century); MF starts -50% from peak
column11: Office deliveries at 4M sf Q4 2025 (lowest since 2012). Pipeline below 20M sf first time in 21st century. MF: 508K delivered 2025, starts at 325K (-50%). Supply correction accelerating.
column22: $63.6B in CMBS 2.0 special servicing. Jan transfers: $2.3B across 38 loans. Office = 59% of January transfers. CMBS 1.0 (legacy pre-2008) at catastrophic 60.87% (mostly zombie loans). CMBS 2.0 crossed 10% threshold = systemic stress level. Special servicing ≠ DQ but leading indicator.

column4: Willis Tower $1.3B + One NY Plaza $835M = $2.1B+ kicked to 2028
column11: NEW RISK VECTOR. Extend-and-pretend creating 2028 maturity cliff. Two known major extensions: Willis Tower (Blackstone, $1.3B, underwater -20%) and One New York Plaza (Brookfield, $835M). Pattern: extend 24 months from 2026 → Jan 2028. If widespread, 2028 becomes new crisis point. Need to quantify: what % of 2026 $936B wall is being kicked to 2028?

EXTREME PRICE DISCOVERY. 600 West Chicago $510M→$89M (-82.6%), 70 West Madison $377M→$80M (-78.6%), 401 North Michigan $360M→$133M (-63.2%), 333 West Wacker $321M→$125M (-61%), 200 South Wacker $215M→$68M (-68.3%). $1.78B→$495M aggregate. ACTUAL SALES, not appraisals. Implies Midwest regional banks face massive reserve builds. Chicago = proxy for secondary/tertiary office markets nationwide.

column4: 271,000 cuts (9% decline, Nov 2025); 317K departed vs 68K hired
column11: RP-CREED-10. LARGEST PEACETIME FEDERAL WORKFORCE CUT ON RECORD. Federal employment at lowest since 1966. 10% reduction in 2025 alone. Net -249K. DC metro gov sector: 727,400 jobs (21.4% of total) — amplification via contractor/services sector (1.5-2x multiplier). PERMANENT structural reduction, not temporary furlough. Ongoing through 2026 (212K+ departed as of Jan 27, 2026). Peak impact on DC CRE expected Q2-Q4 2026 as lease terminations flow through.

RP-CREED-10. Spiked from 20.0% (Q1 2025) → 22.6% (Q2 2025) driven by federal lease terminations. Q2: -395,984 sf negative absorption (federal gov contractions). Q3: 22.4% (slight stabilization from conversions but "office yet to recover"). 600K sf federal lease expirations 2024-2027. GSA consolidation reducing procurement. Federal office utilization 12-14% (crisis-level). Unlike 2013 sequester (temporary), DOGE cuts are permanent + coincide with elevated vacancy + remote work. Prime buildings projected -10.8% value decline 2023-2025. Crosses RED at 25%+ (systemic DC corridor stress).

RP-CREED-10. DC office CRE canary signal. Q4 2024: $74.9M office loan → non-accrual. Q1 2025: NI plunged 89% to $1.7M ($0.06/share) from $15.3M Q4 2024. Q4 2025: partial recovery $7.6M ($0.25/share) but 50% below prior year. Bethesda, MD-based, largest DC community bank, heavy DC office CRE concentration. Stock plunged 2025 on CRE exposure. NPA ratio at 1.04% = ORANGE. Crosses RED at 1.50%+ (credit crisis). Monitor quarterly earnings for trajectory. Peak stress expected Q2-Q4 2026 as DOGE lease terminations hit property cash flows.

RP-CREED-10. Allowance for credit losses to NPL ratio DROPPED 26 bps Q1→Q2 2025 (104.6% → 78.6%). Earnings stable (Q1: $27M, Q2-Q3: $29.7M) but credit quality deteriorating. Alexandria, VA-based, DC corridor concentration. Seeking Alpha rated "HOLD" (Dec 2025) citing "deteriorating loan quality" and CRE risks. $354M LINKBANCORP acquisition (Dec 2025) adds complexity. Coverage below 75% = RED (inadequate reserves for expected losses). Monitor Q4 2025/Q1 2026 for continued deterioration. BHRB stress lagging EGBN but trending worse.

RP-CREED-10. Accelerating: 3M sf in FY2025 alone vs 8M in prior 4 years. 90 properties disposed FY2025. Total GSA: 363M sf nationwide, 90M sf DC area. 8,000+ leases, 50% renewing. CBRE: every 10% GSA space reduction → 20 bps national vacancy increase (DC magnified). DOGE cuts (271K workers) will accelerate terminations 2026-2027. Crosses RED at 5M+ sf/yr (systemic DC market dislocation). Key leading indicator: GSA procurement activity declining (LPC reports reduced smaller lease activity in NCR). Federal utilization 12-14% = massive underutilization driving cuts.

column4: 108.6M sf (C&W Q4 2025); down 20% from Q1 2024 peak
column11: RP-CREED-9. Currently IMPROVING (down 17.5M sf in 2025, 3 consecutive quarterly declines). Major declines: Manhattan -3.8M, San Jose -2.8M, Dallas -1.7M. 60%+ of markets declining YOY. Trades 10-30% below direct lease rates. Competes with Class B/C landlords. Peak was ~130M+ (Q1 2024). Gateway markets stabilizing but still elevated. YELLOW = moderate level, GREEN when <100M sf, ORANGE when >150M (pressure on Class B/C).

column4: -21% (renewals), -32% (new deals) vs pre-pandemic; 40% plan to reduce
column11: RP-CREED-9. H1 2024 data. New deals -32% smaller than pre-pandemic avg. Renewals -21% smaller. 40% of orgs plan to reduce space over next 3 years. Major cases: Fox -13%, Fannie Mae -48%, Cravath -100%. Downsizing rates improving (down 50% from peak) BUT STILL NEGATIVE. Structural demand reduction from hybrid work (avg 3 days/week attendance despite 44% mandating 5 days). Crosses RED at >35% (NOI collapse accelerates, extend-and-pretend fails systemically).
